tasks.gr11-energy-balance-t1: Topic: The Earth's Energy Balance. Cover incoming solar radiation (insolation), the greenhouse effect, albedo, short-wave vs long-wave radiation, and the urban heat island. Ask Grade 11 learners to explain how latitude affects insolation intensity, calculate the effect of albedo on surface temperature, or describe how the energy budget determines Africa's climate.
tasks.gr11-pressure-belts-winds-t1: Topic: Pressure Belts and Winds. Cover the global atmospheric circulation cells (Hadley, Ferrel, Polar), the ITCZ, subtropical high-pressure belts, trade winds, westerlies, the Coriolis effect, and the West African and Indian Ocean monsoons. Ask Grade 11 learners to explain why the Sahara Desert is arid, describe the seasonal migration of the ITCZ, or interpret a diagram of global wind belts.
tasks.gr11-el-nino-la-nina-t1: Topic: El Niño and La Niña. Cover the ENSO cycle, changes in Pacific Ocean trade winds and sea-surface temperatures, El Niño impacts (drought in southern Africa), La Niña impacts (above-normal rainfall), and consequences for agriculture and food security. Ask Grade 11 learners to explain the difference between El Niño and La Niña events, describe the impact on South African rainfall patterns, or evaluate food-security risks.
tasks.gr11-africa-climate-gis-t1: Topic: Africa's Climate Zones, Desertification, and GIS. Cover Africa's major climate zones (equatorial, tropical, desert, Mediterranean, semi-arid), the causes and consequences of desertification in the Sahel, the role of the Benguela Current in creating the Namib Desert, and how GIS and remote sensing are used to monitor climate change and land degradation. Ask Grade 11 learners to interpret a climate graph, explain desertification causes, or describe how satellite imagery supports environmental monitoring.
tasks.gr11-droughts-causes-effects-t1: Topic: Droughts: causes, effects and vulnerability (Grade 11 Geography, Term 1). Cover areas at risk at regional and local scales, natural causes (persistent high pressure, El Nino, climate change) and human causes (overuse of water, loss of vegetation), the effects on people and the environment, and differences in vulnerability. Give all rainfall data in the question. Ask learners to calculate percentage of the mean, deficit or yield loss, or to explain who is most vulnerable.
tasks.gr11-desertification-management-t1: Topic: Desertification: causes, effects and management (Grade 11 Geography, Term 1). Cover what desertification is and where it occurs (the Sahel, the Karoo), causes (overgrazing, overcultivation, cutting trees, poor irrigation, drought), effects on people and the environment, carrying capacity and overstocking sums, and management strategies with case studies (Great Green Wall, farmer-managed tree regrowth). Give all numbers in the question.
tasks.gr11-aerial-photographs-landforms-t1: Topic: Aerial photographs and landforms (Grade 11 Geography, Term 1). Cover vertical and oblique photographs, identifying landforms and features (mesa, butte, cuesta, river valley, built-up area), tone, texture and shadow, and the scale of a vertical photograph. Give all measurements in the question.
tasks.gr11-orthophoto-maps-orienting-t1: Topic: Orthophoto maps: scale, measurement and orientation (Grade 11 Geography, Term 1). Cover what an orthophoto map is, its use with 1:50 000 maps, measuring distance and area at 1:10 000, converting between scales and orienting a photograph with a map. Give all measurements in the question.
